_comment: Per-(binding, backend) whole-graph wallclock around QnnGraph_execute, captured by qnn_models/runtime/profile_segments.cpp on the physical QRB5165 at 10.44.120.201. Every number here is measured; capability-excluded cells are absent by construction (the registry decides those) rather than carrying a sentinel cost.

_notes.fused_full/fused_full_net@cpu: 1147 us is the fp32 graph measured under the cpu lane's own execute mask (taskset -c 4-5, 30 iters) — the mask the runtime actually gives the QNN CPU op package. Unmasked on all 8 cores it measures 1460 us, and on the A55 little cluster 3948 us, so the cell is only meaningful alongside the mask. The earlier 2875 us cell was taken before the exec-mask mechanism existed.
_notes.fused_full/fused_full_net@cpu#contention: In-situ it costs ~5.6x the isolated cell: pooled over 3 reps of the 4-way schedule its exec p50 is 6.39 ms against a 1.147 ms cell (p90 10.2 ms). The per-lane exec mask constrains the lane thread, but the QNN CPU op package's own thread pool is created during bringup on the main thread and keeps full-machine affinity, so it contends with every other lane — including the real-time-gated mlp_control lane. This is the same class as the per-op MILP gap documented in runtime/HETEROGENEOUS_SCHEDULING_QRB5165.md: CPU contention is not in the cost model. dronet (2.50 vs 2.563) and yolov8n (15.55 vs 14.76) sit on their own silicon and match their cells.
_notes.fused_split: Measured under taskset -c 4-5, 40 iters, on the sliced sub-DLCs. The split recovers HTA coverage the monolith could not have (conv branches only) and CPU int8 for both branches, but CPU int8 is only worth taking on the small one: QnnCpu's int8 conv is a reference kernel, 12.2 ms for the vision branch against 0.014 ms for the 8x8 depth branch. The tail runs 0.37 ms on CPU fp32 vs 3.06 ms on DSP.
_notes.vint: Single-shot measurements (n=1) under the performance governor, which is how the runtime dispatches each tile. The cpu cells are fp32 — int8 on CPU is far slower for both tiles (encoders 268.8 ms, decoder 100.6 ms) because QnnCpu's int8 kernels are reference implementations. Whole-network reference: 168.3 ms CPU fp32, 378.5 ms CPU int8, and it composes on no accelerator at all.
_notes.cpu_cells_must_be_unmasked: A CPU cell has to be measured the way the runtime runs it, and the runtime does NOT confine the backend: the lane's exec mask binds the lane thread, but the QNN CPU op package builds its thread pool at bringup on the main thread with full-machine affinity. ViNT's decoder makes the difference impossible to miss — 79-83 ms measured under `taskset -c 4-5`, 12.7 ms unmasked, and 31.3 ms in-situ (sharing the machine with the DSP lane and the control loop). Cells for big multi-threaded CPU graphs are therefore taken unmasked; the masked convention only ever made sense for the tiny ones, where it changes nothing. A pessimistic cell is not harmless: at 83 ms the solver evacuated the CPU lane and put 40 mlp_control instances on the DSP, where they collided with ViNT's encoder and missed 26 of 48 deadlines.
_notes.feedback_does_not_converge_for_contended: The `feedback` stage promotes in-situ medians to cells, which fixes a cell that is wrong for a stable reason (wrong governor, wrong affinity mask). It does NOT converge for a multi-threaded CPU tile, because that tile's cost is a function of what runs beside it. ViNT's decoder went 12.7 ms (standalone, unmasked) -> 37.8 ms (in-situ) -> promoted to a cell -> 12.8 ms in the next run, because the new schedule gave it more of the machine. Measuring changed the schedule, which changed the measurement. Tiles on dedicated silicon do not have this problem: ViNT's encoders hit 1.01x of their DSP cell across every run. Two real fixes exist and neither is a better measurement: model contention explicitly (a per-lane concurrency term), or make the cost load-independent by actually binding the QNN CPU backend's thread pool, which the host runtime cannot do today.
_notes.slicing_study: Cells whose name carries a #study suffix or a *_sliced*/ prefix come from qnn_models/slicing_study (RESULTS.md), a granularity sweep over five networks. They are appended, not substituted: the statistic differs from the rest of this file. Each is the MEDIAN of profile_seg's per-sweep median over 1-2 sweeps, under the performance governor, with CPU cells UNMASKED, 20-200 iters depending on graph size -- the median because two other workers share the board and a CPU sweep occasionally catches a contention spike (fused t0's CPU mean moved 0.44 -> 1.51 ms between sweeps while its median moved 0.44 -> 0.61). cpu@fp32 keys are the fp32 build of the same graph, kept alongside the int8 cpu cell because the better precision is a per-tile decision: CPU int8 beats fp32 4x on ViNT's encoders and loses 5x on dronet and 7x on ViNT's decoder. Three results here revise notes elsewhere in this file. (1) Resize DOES compose on HTA: yolov8n_sliced3/yolov8n_t0_op0_136 contains both FPN Resize ops, three MaxPool and eight residual Add and runs at 15.6 ms on HTA; the real blocker in the detect head is the Transpose the converter emits for its Reshape ops. (2) The shipped yolov8n cut at op 102 is 34 ops earlier than HTA requires -- op 136 is the last op before the first layout change. (3) No yolov8n tile reaches HTA at ANY granularity without the offline Split -> 2x Conv1x1 rewrite (optimizations.md #14); sliced from yolov8n.onnx directly, both the whole net and the backbone are rejected with 'unsupported op Split'. Measured per-dispatch overhead, from synthetic 1-MAC probes (label overhead_probe): DSP 0.367 ms, HTA 0.540 ms (median; 0.26 min, 2.96 p99), CPU 0.0026 ms. Confirmed against real cuts: an extra DSP dispatch costs 0.37 ms + 5.4 ns per byte of boundary tensor, which is why dronet (3 KB boundary) pays 0.37 ms per cut and yolov8n (717 KB) pays 4.4 ms.

conditions.cpu_affinity: taskset -c 4-5 for cpu cells (the lane's exec mask)
conditions.why: Cells must be measured in the state the run executes in. Under schedutil the board idles at 710 MHz of 2419 and the accelerator cells come out 10-36% pessimistic — the host clock gates FastRPC dispatch, so DSP and HTA work is measured slow when the CPU is slow (yolov8n backbone on HTA: 21.6 ms under schedutil, 13.9 ms under performance). The previous cells are kept in _previous_cells_schedutil for comparison.
conditions.sweep_variance: Three independent 20-iteration sweeps under the same governor, same board, minutes apart: dronet@hta 1.96/2.01/1.61, yolov8n_backbone@dsp 13.10/12.83/12.24, yolov8n_head@dsp 15.82/15.94/16.08, mlp_control@cpu 0.10/0.09/0.03 ms. So a cell carries roughly +-10% of sweep-to-sweep spread (much more for sub-100us graphs, where the measurement is noise-dominated), which is the floor on prediction accuracy unless cells are taken as a median of repeated sweeps. The one systematic residual is yolov8n's head: every sweep puts it at 15.4-16.5 ms while in-situ it is consistently 17.2-17.3 ms, and single-shot measurement (N=1) gives 17.2 — the runtime dispatches each tile once per instance, not in a loop, so for this graph the loop mean is the wrong statistic.
